# PR #256 performance review

Head: 695aae4a4033941c44dfead656ef070febf9fef9
Result: PASS WITH NOTES. No measured normal-use runtime cost breach. This performance verdict does not clear the correctness review's audit-metric finding or the pending Refuse/Warn ruling. Round 1 under C34; no local builds or tests.

## Runtime cost

- TTL enrichment reuses the existing SessionStatusPort read. `session_status_block` fills facts from the already-resolved descriptor; `fill_cache_ttl` checks at most five static rows, with no I/O, subprocess, timer, or transcript reread. Unisphere's existing per-seat incremental cursor, serialized read, 30-second cached misses, and explicit Copilot transcript path are unchanged (`crates/unisphere/src/lib.rs:209-296`). There was already one status read per guarded send; no additional transcript read was introduced.
- Existing PA cadence stays 60 seconds. Its bounded fleet reads now clone a complete SeatDescriptor per admitted seat read, rather than only id/harness/session; list sizing similarly clones descriptors per local row per requested sized list. Both remain O(seats) per existing pass, with extra bounded metadata copying. There is no new steady-state launch per tick per seat. TTL/basis display also adds small string formatting work; 'no new work' would be inaccurate.
- Qualification to the PR's 'no added reads/launches': `http/cold_wake.rs:135-145` can now enter the existing stale-working check for a large working seat idle between its short TTL and one hour. This adds an existing `seat.activity` lookup on those newly eligible sends. If the working activity itself is older than one hour, the existing pane probe also runs. Capture normally rides the persistent tmux control client; its existing counted capture-pane fork fallback remains possible when that client is unavailable (`crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:456-461,1098-1104`). No new executable site was added, but unchanged sites do not prove unchanged invocation counts. This is conditional per-send work, not a new periodic loop.

## Live receipts

Production remained on 408418a18c, PID 34653. Two `pij-rs --json ping` readings at epoch seconds 1795062442.444748 and 1795062462.783172 observed total spawns 1763 -> 1763; every by_op delta was zero over 20.3384 seconds. `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` exited 0: whole-machine 284.6 launches/s, sampled 274.4/s, no daemon children observed. Sampling attribution is a lower bound; the machine rate is not attributable to this PR. Independent daemon snapshots showed 32.2% then 18.2% CPU and RSS 125680 then 127152 KiB; these are snapshots, not isolated CPU-cost deltas. This is BEFORE evidence only, not a deployed-head comparison.

On-demand smoke: `/usr/bin/time -lp just cache-ttl-audit /tmp/f214/fr-all --json /tmp/f214/performance-256-695aae4.json`, exit 0. Existing seven-day report plus live read-only store: 14620 deliveries, 13404 paired, 9402 decided. Wall 12.18 s; user 4.11 s; system 1.62 s; maximum RSS 175128576 bytes; swaps 0. Recipe runs Python at nice 19, outside the daemon, with no subprocess calls inside the script. It read 93,599,153 bytes of report call metadata and traversed 182 full Copilot logs totaling 3,475,242,045 bytes, extracting usage metadata only. The SQLite file was 2,482,364,416 bytes. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reports SCAN spine_events for each of its three spine queries: three full logical scans, not indexed time-window seeks. Physical disk bytes were not measured. Complexity includes those history scans, full selected transcript sizes, and a per-delivery O(calls-in-seat) temporary timestamp list at audit.py:150. Acceptable as the measured explicit command; not appropriate as a poll or periodic sensor without separate cost review.

## Measurement correctness: do not use the headline totals as guard outcomes

The committed script reproduces the PR's 785 -> 47 silent-cold and 33 -> 221 false-cold totals, but stats() mixes cache warmth with send-guard decisions. Recounting its saved rows using actual guard outcomes gives silent cold 970 -> 710 across all sizes; large-only 265 -> 5 remains correct. Warm-seat refusals are 4 -> 56, not 33 -> 221. Of the reported 221, 165 are small seats whose guard says clear. All 52 newly refused warm large seats have their own 300-second TTL (32 Copilot, 20 OMP), not a table-only TTL. The correctness reviewer independently corroborated these counts and owns disposition. In particular, do not report 221 sender refusals or a 785 -> 47 all-seat guard improvement. No fleet_report* or prompt-cache-cost.md changes are present in this PR.

CI run 44457705817 succeeded at the exact reviewed head. Local review ran only read-only production measurements, audit smoke and metadata recount; no local build, test, install, bounce, or source modification.

## Owed after deployment

Owner: role:performance (#256), carried durably in this verdict and role memory. After merge and bounce, record the deployed commit/time/PID; repeat the paired spawn counters, 20-second machine probe and daemon CPU/RSS observation. After at least three days, generate a two-thread fleet report starting at the deployment time, run the audit, verify guard-only outcome totals rather than the mixed cache-state totals, inspect warn receipts and forced-wake cache_ttl/basis events, and publish `f214-audit-after` to pm-001. Reconstructed outcomes are not recorded sender decisions; a refused delivery has no observed next-call counterfactual, so do not equate replay with measured false-refusal rate. No after-deploy improvement is claimed yet.

Local receipts: /tmp/f214/performance-256-cost-before.json and /tmp/f214/performance-256-695aae4.json. No message bodies or credentials are included in these output artifacts.
